note: SG-81. Per-MODEL-KEY light accents, read by scripts/view3d.gd (the MODEL LIGHTS region) and applied to every live instance of the key. Edited in the lab: SkyGear Tools.bat lab, LIGHTS mode, SAVE writes this file. offset/range are GROUND UNITS; offset is in the model's own frame, +Y up, +Z the face it shows the camera. type omni|spot; spot adds angle (degrees, half-cone) and aim. hz/depth/shape are the optional throb - shape pulse is a clean sine, flicker is a fire. Energy is clamped to MODEL_LIGHT_MAX_ENERGY and range to MODEL_LIGHT_MAX_RANGE at read time, and the nearest MODEL_LIGHT_CAP within MODEL_LIGHT_ENERGY_BUDGET are the ones that actually light.

boss._note: SG-90, re-judged at SG-94. WHY IT IS A LIGHT: the part-segmentation export the Colossus was first cut from is a VISUALISATION with no UVs and no maps, so the furnace grate the prompted Colossus carried in an emission map had nowhere to go. It became a light instead - the same read from the same place, at the torso's own front centre (measured off assets/models/boss/parts.json, not guessed), on the furnace knight's flicker, bigger and slower because it is a bigger furnace. SG-94 MARRIED THE TEXTURED TWIN IN and the machine now wears real maps, so this row was re-measured rather than assumed. IT STAYS, AND AT THIS ENERGY. (1) The twin's emission map does NOT replace it: mean 0.2/255 with 0.17% of pixels lit, which is a few small vents and not a furnace. (2) It is not washing the new paint out - the blown fraction of the frame is 0.043% at energy 0.0 and 0.043% at 2.00, so nothing the lamp does clips. (3) It saturates just about here: measured with the flicker held still (tools/boss_shot.gd, a sweep), it lifts 2.7% of the frame at 0.60, 4.9% at this 1.28 and 5.7% at 2.00 - so raising it buys under a percentage point of lit area for 56% more of a shared MODEL_LIGHT_ENERGY_BUDGET, and lowering it to 0.90 costs a measurable part of the machine's read.
